skill.name: github-cli
skill.description: Encourages proactive use of GitHub CLI (gh) for gathering context on PRs, issues, comments, and repository information when working with GitHub-related tasks.
skill.summary: Guides assistants to use GitHub CLI for pull requests, issues, reviews, CI status, and repository context.
skill.author: BfdCampos

security_audit.summary: The skill is a GitHub CLI guidance document, not executable code, but it repeatedly instructs assistants to run authenticated external commands and GitHub API requests. The command usage is mostly read-only and legitimate for GitHub context gathering, while the sample hardcoded URLs are benign examples. No prompt injection text or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running gh commands against private repositories, user-supplied URLs, or broad API endpoints.
Prefer read-only high-level gh commands and document that write, delete, workflow, and secret-related endpoints require explicit user approval.
Add instructions to avoid sharing PR comments, issue discussions, repository metadata, or CI details outside the user's requested context.

content.value_statement: GitHub work often needs PR, issue, and CI context that local git cannot show. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use GitHub CLI for that context.
actual_capabilities: Guides assistants to inspect pull request details, diffs, comments, reviews, and CI checks with gh.
Provides issue workflows for viewing issue details, comments, lists, and search results.
Shows repository context commands for branches, releases, workflow runs, and repository metadata.
Explains how to turn GitHub pull request and issue URLs into gh commands with repo scopes.
Encourages combining local git history with GitHub discussion context before reviewing code.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI to be installed and authenticated in the user environment.
Depends on repository permissions for private PRs, issues, comments, and workflow data.
Focuses on context gathering and does not provide a full GitHub automation framework.
Does not include detailed guardrails for write operations or broad GitHub API calls.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Gather PR descriptions, diffs, checks, review comments, and discussion before analyzing a change.

use_cases.title: Investigate Issues
use_cases.description: Read issue details and comments so bug triage includes the full GitHub conversation.

use_cases.title: Check Repository Activity
use_cases.description: Inspect branches, releases, workflow runs, and repository metadata during development or release support.

prompt_templates.title: View PR Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to gather context for PR 123 in the current repository. Summarize the description, changed files, CI status, and open review comments.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate an Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GitHub CLI context gathering for issue 456. Read the issue body and comments, then summarize the problem, affected users, and likely next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Find GitHub context for my current branch. Identify linked pull requests, recent CI status, unresolved comments, and any related issue discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Review Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Before reviewing this repository change, combine local git history with GitHub PR context. Report discussion themes, failing checks, risky files, and reviewer concerns.

output_examples.input: Review PR 123 before I make changes.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes the PR purpose, changed areas, CI status, unresolved comments, and review concerns before suggesting code work.
The assistant reports the issue status, key comments, labels, participants, and recommended follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Check whether my branch is ready for review.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies linked PRs, branch status, recent checks, and remaining discussion points that may block review.

best_practices: Confirm repository scope before running gh commands outside the current repository.
Use structured gh output when the response needs reliable fields from PRs, issues, reviews, or checks.
Read GitHub discussion context before making code recommendations for collaborative work.
anti_patterns: Do not assume local git history includes PR comments, issue discussion, or CI state.
Do not run broad GitHub API calls when a scoped gh command answers the question.
Do not expose private repository details beyond the user's requested task.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides assistants to use GitHub CLI for PRs, issues, reviews, CI checks, and repository context.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The environment needs gh installed and authenticated for the target repositories.

faq.question: Can it work with private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, if the authenticated GitHub account has permission to view the requested repository data.

faq.question: Does it change GitHub data?
faq.answer: The documented examples are read-focused. Users should approve any write, delete, workflow, or secret-related action.

faq.question: How does it help code review?
faq.answer: It brings PR descriptions, diffs, comments, reviews, and checks into the assistant's analysis.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
